newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares set year-high in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares set year-high in active trading.

text.p: Shanghai B shares set a year-high of 56.440 points and ended at a year-closing high of 56.114 points on Monday in active trading, mainly of smaller, cheaper stocks, on good market sentiment, brokers said.
The index surged 2.693 points or 5.04 percent to 56.114 points, on volume of 28.2 million shares worth $10.6 million. All 42 B shares traded, with 41 up and one flat.

Brokers said that investors were encouraged by the index breaching the 55-point resistance level and buying focussed on smaller, lower priced stocks whose prices were far below their net capital per share.
"Market sentiment has improved greatly on recent surges in the Shenzhen B share market and the market is bullish in the short term," one broker said.
"Technical charts indicate the index is likely to test the 60-point level despite minor technical corrections from time to time," another broker said.
Wing Sung was the star on speculative buying, surging $0.050 or 27.77 percent to $0.230, on volume of 71,000 shares.
Shanghai Vacuum Electron Device followed on bargain-hunting, up $0.022 or 15.94 percent to $0.160, on volume of 685,600 shares.
Shanghai Huili Building Material traded the most, rising $0.018 or 9.57 percent to $0.206, on volume of 3.0 million shares.
Shanghai A share index reached its highest level in three years, with record trading volume of 16.7 billion yuan, due to fresh inflow of capital from Shenzhen, brokers said.

The A index surged 108.009 points or 9.94 percent to 1,194.090 points, on volume of 1.9 billion shares worth 16.7 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index jumped 197.146 points or 7.64 percent to 2779.052 points.
Chengdu Measuring and Cutting Tools was the star on institutional buying, soaring 1.54 yuan or 27.79 percent to 7.08 yuan, on volume of 16.0 million shares.
